behavioral_effects: MANUAL_STEPS.md: new checklist item requiring docker model status to show llama.cpp Running with a -cuda tag, with the nv-gpu-info.exe fix (docker/model-runner#1054); the Taskiq line now states the measured 7.5 GB GPU footprint instead of until measured.
docs/file-processing.md Embedding Providers: documents that Model Runner shares the GPU with Docling Serve, the measured footprint, and the CUDA OOM remedies.
compatibility_impact: None to repository contracts. The host-side change moved Docker Model Runner llama.cpp from the stale latest-cuda build (ac4cdde, June 2026) to the pinned b9879-cuda build (72874f5). The ADR-002 embedding contract was re-verified: the same input yields the same 2560-d native vector (cosine 1.0 against the pre-change vector) and identical rerank scores.
follow_up: Extend preflight-model to parse docker model status so a backend install Error is caught by the registered health check; it went unnoticed for two months because the request path kept working.
The model-runner maintainer states the project is being deprecated in favour of llmman (no public repo yet); ADR-005 models Model Runner as a host runtime and will need revisiting when that lands.
limitations: Additive documentation: the only removal was the obsolete until-measured clause; the shrink pass cut one remedy sentence that was duplicated between the two files.
The fix is host-side and recurs: the b9879-cuda backend image ships without com.docker.nv-gpu-info.exe, so the copy must be repeated after every Docker Desktop llama.cpp bump; nothing automates it.

The new llama.cpp build does not print a CUDA0 device line into docker model logs on model load; GPU serving was verified with --list-devices on the new binary and nvidia-smi (7.6 GB used with both models warm).
reason: Docker Desktop 4.82 and later stop provisioning com.docker.nv-gpu-info.exe into the per-user inference directory, so the llama.cpp backend has reported an install Error since 2026-08-12 while serving from a stale June CUDA build, and nothing in the docs that describe the Model Runner dependency mentions the check or the fix, so the next operator re-diagnoses it from scratch. The same docs also lack the measured GPU footprint: a warm Qwen3 4B embedder plus reranker take the 8 GB GPU to about 7.5 GB, which Docling Serve shares.
risks: If the helper copy is forgotten after a llama.cpp bump, docker model status regresses to Error while serving continues on the previously installed build.
rollback: git revert restores both docs. It does not restore the host: the previous CUDA llama.cpp install is preserved at C:\Users\pollm\.docker\bin\inference.bak-2026-10-12 (951 MiB) and can be renamed back over .docker\bin\inference while no model is loaded; the copied com.docker.nv-gpu-info.exe lives outside the repo.
security_impact: None. Documentation only. The documented host-side procedure copies a Docker Desktop-shipped executable into the user profile and changes no exposure, secret, or MCP surface.
summary: Document the Docker Model Runner nv-gpu-info.exe provisioning fix and the DMR/Docling GPU memory contention
